title: fix(objectql,runtime): install datasourceMapping before the first schema sync, so a mapped boot keeps one store (#23649)
body:
Fixes #23649

Clause-②: yes

## What was wrong

A host config declaring `datasourceMapping: [{ default: true, datasource: 'primary' }]` over a declared SQLite `primary` booted to `Server is ready` and then answered `no such table` on every platform read. `AppPlugin.start()` installed the rules (`ql.setDatasourceMapping`) after `ObjectQLPlugin.start()` had schema-synced every registered object onto the host's default store, and after the auth plugin had written the Default Organization there. From that moment the engine routed every unbound object to `primary` (step 2 of `resolveDatasourceBinding`), and `primary`'s schema had never been synced.

The same late install had a second form. The connect gate (ADR-0062 D2 (d)) counted only the app's own objects. A rule that routes only platform objects (`objectPattern: 'sys_*'`, the spec's own example shape) therefore never connected its datasource at all. Every platform read then failed with "mapped for object ... is not registered".

## Honour or refuse: measured first

Triage left the choice open, with one guard: if honouring the mapping changes which store a config that boots correctly today resolves to, stop and return the fork. Honouring changes nothing for any such config I could build, so this PR honours the mapping. The readings are below.

Every boot used the built CLI (`bin/run.js`) with `NODE_ENV` unset (production), `OS_AUTH_SECRET` set and `OS_CLOUD_URL=off`. Each store was opened read-only after the process exited. "Before" means `origin/main` at `57994c311` for the host-config rows. For the rows marked (a), it means this branch with the fix's one subscription line removed and `packages/runtime` rebuilt, which makes the boot behave exactly as before the change. "After" means this branch at `4c64e2aed`.

Boots that work today. All of them are unchanged:

| shape | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| CONTROL: no mapping, `OS_DATABASE_URL=file:ctl.db` | ready, 0 errors; `ctl.db` 72 tables, 1 organization | identical |
| `default: true` to the host's own `default` | ready, 0 errors; `ctl.db` 72 tables, 1 organization | identical |
| `default: true` to `primary`, with `OS_DATABASE_URL` set to `primary`'s own file | ready, 0 errors; one file, 72 tables, 1 organization | identical |
| `os start` on the config-declared default (`default: true` to `primary`, no URL), which is the shape the shared resolver honours (a) | ready, 0 errors; `ds-primary.db` 72 tables, 1 organization | identical |
| M9: a stack plugin registers a SQL `driver.*` service in `init()`, plus a declared `archive` with `autoConnect`, no mapping, no URL | ready, 0 errors; default driver `com.objectstack.driver.sql`; plugin store 72 tables, 1 organization; `archive` 0 tables | identical, same default driver |
| `objectPattern: 'fx_*'` to `primary` (the app's own object only), URL set | ready, 0 errors; `fx_task` rows served from `primary`; `ctl.db` also held an empty `fx_task` table from the first sync | ready, 0 errors; `fx_task` on `primary` only, so `ctl.db` has 71 tables |
| M5: `default: true` to `primary`, production, no URL | refused by the no-storage guard | identical |

The one difference among these is that empty `fx_task` copy: the first sync no longer creates it in a store the object never routes to. No row moves. The rules were already in force for every write once `start()` had run, and app seeds run after that point.

Boots that are broken today:

| shape | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| M7: `default: true` to `primary`, `OS_DATABASE_URL=file:ctl.db` | ready, then 61 `DATABASE_ERROR ... no such table`; `ctl.db` 72 tables and the organization, `primary` 13 tables and no organization | ready, 0 errors; `primary` 71 tables and 1 organization; `ctl.db` holds `sys_packages` only (see the acceptance notes) |
| M8: the same config with `--dev` | ready, then 63 `DATABASE_ERROR`; `primary` 13 tables, no organization | ready, 0 errors; `primary` 71 tables and 1 organization |
| `os start` on the same config with `OS_DATABASE_URL=file:ctl.db` (a) | ready, then 61 `DATABASE_ERROR`; split as in M7 | ready, 0 errors; `primary` 71 tables and 1 organization |
| `objectPattern: 'sys_*'` to `primary`, URL set | ready, then 36 "is not registered"; `primary` never connected | ready, 0 errors; `primary` 70 tables and 1 organization; `fx_task` stays in `ctl.db` |
| M9 with `default: true` to `archive` | ready, then 61 `DATABASE_ERROR`; split | ready, 0 errors; `archive` 71 tables and 1 organization; the default driver is still the plugin's |
| `objectPattern: 'sys_*'` to a declared postgres that refuses connections (a) | ready, then 38 "is not registered" | refused at boot: `[AppPlugin] declared-datasource auto-connect failed for app ...: datasource 'primary': connect failed — connect ECONNREFUSED ... (70 object(s) are routed to it by a datasourceMapping rule ...)` |

The last row is the one boot this change refuses that used to print a banner. The published contract already says so: `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx` says "If a `datasourceMapping` rule routes an object to a datasource that cannot be connected, the boot **fails** with the connect error". The published `skills/objectstack-data/rules/datasources.md` says the same ("A rule pointing at a datasource that cannot be connected fails the boot"), and so does ADR-0062's #4462 amendment ("a `declared-auto` failure is **fatal**"). The implementation counted only the app's objects, so it never reached that refusal for platform objects. The seat ruled this refusal is the implementation pulled back to the published declaration (review 6196599954, answer A), so it is not a narrowing. The declaration's `yes` is owed by the widening below, not by this refusal.

## What changed

**Public surface (why the declaration reads `yes`).** `@objectstack/objectql` gains one entry export, `OBJECTQL_DRIVERS_READY_HOOK`, and `ObjectQLPlugin.start()` triggers one new kernel event, `objectql:drivers-ready`, which any plugin can subscribe to. The changeset bumps `@objectstack/objectql` `minor` for it; `@objectstack/runtime` stays `patch`.

- **`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`.** `ObjectQLPlugin.start()` triggers `objectql:drivers-ready` (exported as `OBJECTQL_DRIVERS_READY_HOOK`) once per boot, with the engine as its argument. It fires after `driver.*` adoption and `ObjectQL.init()`, and before the first `installRegisteredSchemas`, the `sys_metadata` hydration and any read or write. A throwing handler propagates and fails the boot. The call site spells the name as the literal `'objectql:drivers-ready'`, because the settings bind-window guard derives the hooks fired before the settings bind from their call sites and reads only a literal. The event is such a hook, so it is pinned in that guard's `PRE_BIND_HOOKS` with its fire site (`scripts/check-settings-bind-window.mjs`, the guard's own prescribed remedy). Its one handler, AppPlugin's, reads no setting. The runtime pin subscribes through the exported constant, so it goes red if the literal and the constant ever differ.
- **`packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts`.** `AppPlugin.init()` subscribes to that event. The handler, `honourDatasourceMappingBeforeSchemaSync`, installs the rules. It then calls the same `connectDeclared` that `start()` uses, for every declared datasource the rules route an already-registered object to. That set is asked of the engine's own matcher (`resolveMappedObjects` over `ql.registry.getAllObjects()`), platform objects included. The fail-fast verdict and the error line are the same as `start()`'s. `start()` installs the rules only when nothing announced the pre-sync moment, for example a declaration-only boot that suppresses the engine plugin's start, or a mock context with no hook bus.
- The connect still happens after the engine has adopted its `driver.*` services. That is the readings' M9 concern: the engine makes its first registered driver the default, so an `init()`-time connect would have taken the default slot from a stack plugin's driver. The M9 rows above show the default driver unchanged.

**Landing point:** the boot order, as triage expected. The announcement lives in `packages/objectql`, and the install and connect live in the runtime `AppPlugin`, cross-lane on the claim's declared surface. `resolveDatasourceBinding`'s order is unchanged, because the defect was when the rules arrived, not the order.

## Tests

- `packages/runtime/src/datasource-mapping-before-schema-sync.test.ts` (new, in-process): the served host composition with a real SQL default driver, the engine plugin, a fixture platform plugin that registers an object the app does not declare and writes a row in `start()` (the Default Organization's slot), the app, and the datasource-admin plugin with the real driver factory. All stores are `:memory:`. It checks three legs: `default: true` (the table and the boot row are on `primary`, and neither is on the default store), `sys_*` (`primary` is connected and holds the platform object, and the app object stays on the default store), and the no-mapping CONTROL (everything on the default store, `primary` metadata-only). Every leg also asserts that the default driver is the `DriverPlugin`'s. Result: 3 passed.
- `packages/cli/test/serve-datasource-mapping-before-sync.integration.test.ts` (new, integration tier, run with `--project integration`): the M7 shape at the public door, two production boots of the built CLI. Mapped: the banner, no "no such table" and no "is not registered", `primary` holds `sys_organization` (1 row), `sys_metadata`, `sys_user` and `fx_task`, and `ctl.db` has no `sys_organization` and no `sys_metadata`. CONTROL: everything in `ctl.db`, and `ds-primary.db` is never created. Result: 2 passed (17.6 s, so it declares a `test-budget` of 30).
- Affected-package suites at `4c64e2aed`: `@objectstack/runtime` 389 files and 5862 tests passed (19 skipped), and `@objectstack/objectql` 422 files and 8118 tests passed.
- After merging `origin/main` (`09dd53719`), at `18baa1fce`, with the CLI closure rebuilt (61 turbo tasks): `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql run typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime run typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli run typecheck` each exit 0; runtime pin 3 passed; CLI pin (`--project integration`) 2 passed. The probe on the merged build reads the same as above for M7, CONTROL, `os start` on the config-declared default, `sys_*` and the unreachable `sys_*` target. The final commit `4b45f9957` adds only the child-env census line (see Gates), which neither the typechecks nor the pins read.
- Round 2, at `700a1bf30` (`origin/main` merged again at `f77ba411e`; #23687 had changed `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` in its metadata-event bridge, a region disjoint from the start-order lines this PR edits): `objectql` rebuilt, and the dist carries the literal fire site once. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql run typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime run typecheck` exit 0. Runtime pin 3 passed. CLI pin (`--project integration`) 2 passed. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-settings-ordering.pin.test.ts`, which names the edited guard, passed. Suites: `@objectstack/objectql` 425 files and 8134 tests passed, `@objectstack/runtime` 389 files and 5866 tests passed (19 skipped).

**Ablation (negative control).** I committed the fix first, then removed the one subscription line in `AppPlugin.init()` (`ctx.hook(OBJECTQL_DRIVERS_READY_HOOK, ...)`) with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 to 0, blob changed) and rebuilt `packages/runtime`. `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs --absent` showed the marker absent from all 6 built files. Results with the line removed:
- runtime pin: 2 failed and 1 passed (CONTROL). The failures were `expected [ 'fx_task' ] to include 'sys_fx_ledger'` and `a datasource only platform objects route to was never connected`.
- CLI pin: 1 failed and 1 passed (CONTROL). The failure was `a platform read hit an unsynced datasource ... not to contain 'no such table'`.

The tool restored the line (blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty). I then rebuilt, the preflight showed the marker present in `dist/index.js`, and both pins passed again.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran` at `700a1bf30`, every command run on that tree with its exit code recorded: 87 derived, 87 run, 0 NOT MEASURED, and all 87 exit 0. In the first pass, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET, unbuilt packages); its re-run after the list measured and passed. CI on `700a1bf30`: 40 check-runs, 34 success, 6 skipped, none failed; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are all green.

**The red this round fixed.** CI on `4b45f9957` and `3a70801fc` failed one gate, `Settings bind-window guard` (`pnpm check:settings-bind-window`). It refused the fire site `ctx.trigger(OBJECTQL_DRIVERS_READY_HOOK, this.ql)` because it cannot name a hook given through a constant. Locally the gate exits 1 on `3a70801fc` and 0 on `origin/main` `f77ba411e`, so the red was this branch's own. Round 1's local derivation did not name that gate: it was not among the 86 families. It derives now because its script is edited. The fix is the literal fire site plus the `PRE_BIND_HOOKS` row above. The gate now reads 9 pre-bind hooks fired, all 9 pinned.

Census and pin edits in gate scripts, both forced by this change and both the gate's own prescribed remedy: `scripts/check-cli-test-child-env.mjs` names the new production-posture `bin/run.js` spawner (eight files to nine; its self-test passes 152 cases), and `scripts/check-settings-bind-window.mjs` pins `objectql:drivers-ready`. Families CI runs beyond this list are read from the check-runs above.

## Acceptance notes

- **`sys_packages` stays on the default driver.** The package registry's table is not an object, and `service-package` deliberately creates and reads it on the engine's default driver (`package-table.ts` says why). Under a `default: true` rule with a separate URL store, that table is the one thing left in the URL store (M7 after: `ctl.db` holds `sys_packages` only). It is read and written consistently there. Noted, not filed. Carrier: none.
- **ADR-0062's Phase 1 implementation note** says declared datasources are auto-connected from `AppPlugin.start()`. Mapping targets now connect at `objectql:drivers-ready`, which is earlier and still AppPlugin's code. The ADR's decision text (D2 (d): "a datasource a mapping rule routes at least one registered object to is auto-connected at boot") is what this implements. The note is left alone because `docs/adr/**` is a governed surface. Carrier: none.
- **`objectql:drivers-ready` is not in `IPluginLifecycleEvents`.** Custom names are legal on the bus, and the registry is in `packages/spec`, which is outside this claim. Carrier: none.
- **Where an unopenable-SQLite hang surfaces now.** A declared sqlite datasource whose file cannot be created (I measured a path under `/proc`) hangs its connect until the plugin start timeout. Before this change, a mapping-routed one timed out as the app plugin's start (30 s). Now it times out as the engine plugin's start (120 s), because the connect moved into that start. Neither message names the datasource. The hang predates this change. Filed follow-up: #23696.
